title: Cohomology in a weak Serre class gives a triangulated subcategory
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category and let $D(\mathcal A)$ and $H^q$ be its derived category and cohomology functors [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $\mathcal B$ be a strictly full subcategory of $\mathcal A$ containing zero, containing the kernels and cokernels in $\mathcal A$ of all morphisms between its objects, and closed under extensions: if $0\to B_1\to E\to B_2\to0$ is short exact with $B_1,B_2\in\mathcal B$, then $E\in\mathcal B$. The full subcategory $D_{\mathcal B}(\mathcal A)$ of objects $K$ with $H^q(K)\in\mathcal B$ for every $q\in\mathbf Z$ is a strictly full triangulated subcategory of $D(\mathcal A)$. Its intersections with $D^+(\mathcal A)$ and $D^b(\mathcal A)$ [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories] are also full triangulated subcategories with the inherited shifts and distinguished triangles. Here full triangulated subcategory has the inherited structure of [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory].

source.place: Tag 06UQ, label lemma-cohomology-in-serre-subcategory, derived.tex:5935-5960, including the bounded versions; hypotheses expanded using homology.tex:2148-2171, Tag 0754, label lemma-characterize-weak-serre-subcategory (weak Serre definition: Tag 02MO, label definition-serre-subcategory).

proof.text: The chosen subcategory is full by construction. If $K\cong L$, functoriality gives $H^q(K)\cong H^q(L)$ for every $q$; strict fullness of $\mathcal B$ therefore makes membership invariant under isomorphism. The zero complex has zero cohomology, so its image in the derived category belongs to $D_{\mathcal B}(\mathcal A)$.

source.place: Tag 06UQ, label lemma-cohomology-in-serre-subcategory, proof; hypotheses expanded by Homology Tag 0754, label lemma-characterize-weak-serre-subcategory

proof.text: For every $k,q\in\mathbf Z$, the cohomology-shift isomorphism is $H^q(K[k])\cong H^{q+k}(K)$. Hence if $K$ belongs to $D_{\mathcal B}(\mathcal A)$, then so does $K[k]$, by strict fullness of $\mathcal B$. The argument includes negative shifts, since $q\mapsto q+k$ permutes all integer degrees.

source.place: Tag 06UQ, label lemma-cohomology-in-serre-subcategory, proof; hypotheses expanded by Homology Tag 0754, label lemma-characterize-weak-serre-subcategory

proof.text: Let $X\to Y\to Z\to X[1]$ be a distinguished triangle with $X,Z\in D_{\mathcal B}(\mathcal A)$. For each $q$, take its five consecutive cohomology terms $H^{q-1}(Z)\xrightarrow{a}H^q(X)\xrightarrow{b}H^q(Y)\xrightarrow{c}H^q(Z)\xrightarrow{d}H^{q+1}(X)$. They are exact at the three inner positions. All four outer terms belong to $\mathcal B$.

source.place: Tag 06UQ, label lemma-cohomology-in-serre-subcategory, proof; hypotheses expanded by Homology Tag 0754, label lemma-characterize-weak-serre-subcategory

proof.text: Put $U=\operatorname{coker}a$ and $V=\ker d$. Exactness gives $\ker b=\operatorname{im}a$, $\ker c=\operatorname{im}b$, and $\operatorname{im}c=\ker d$. Thus the map induced by $b$ embeds $U$ into $H^q(Y)$: $U\cong\operatorname{coim}b$ by the cokernel universal property, and the coimage-to-target map is mono by the cited lemma. Its image is $\operatorname{im}b=\ker c$. The factor of $c$ through $V=\operatorname{im}c$ is the epimorphism onto its image; its kernel is still $\ker c$, because $V\to H^q(Z)$ is mono. This gives the short exact sequence $0\to U\to H^q(Y)\to V\to0$. These are the kernel, image and cokernel identifications in an abelian category, applied to the displayed exact row, not an appeal to weak-Serre closure as an extra theorem.

source.place: Tag 06UQ, label lemma-cohomology-in-serre-subcategory, proof; hypotheses expanded by Homology Tag 0754, label lemma-characterize-weak-serre-subcategory

proof.text: The map $a$ is between two objects of $\mathcal B$, so its cokernel $U$ belongs to $\mathcal B$. Likewise $d$ is between two objects of $\mathcal B$, so its kernel $V$ belongs to $\mathcal B$. Apply precisely the extension hypothesis of the item to the short exact sequence just constructed: $H^q(Y)\in\mathcal B$. Since $q$ was arbitrary, $Y\in D_{\mathcal B}(\mathcal A)$. This writes out the five-term weak-Serre implication of Homology 02MO/0754 for the row used here.

source.place: Tag 06UQ, label lemma-cohomology-in-serre-subcategory, proof; hypotheses expanded by Homology Tag 0754, label lemma-characterize-weak-serre-subcategory

proof.text: The full subcategory contains zero, is stable under every shift, and contains the middle vertex of each distinguished triangle whose outer vertices belong to it. The full-triangulated-subcategory criterion supplies the inherited shift and distinguished triangles and makes it triangulated, since $D(\mathcal A)$ is triangulated. Its strict fullness was proved in step 1.

source.place: Tag 06UQ, label lemma-cohomology-in-serre-subcategory, proof; hypotheses expanded by Homology Tag 0754, label lemma-characterize-weak-serre-subcategory

proof.text: For each $E=D^+(\mathcal A)$ and $E=D^b(\mathcal A)$, the cited bounded-derived-category node states that $E$ contains zero, is stable under shifts, and contains the third vertex whenever it contains two vertices of a distinguished triangle. The intersection $E\cap D_{\mathcal B}(\mathcal A)$ is full and contains zero. A shift preserves each factor, hence preserves their intersection. If the outer vertices of a triangle belong to the intersection, its middle vertex belongs to $E$ by the cited closure and to $D_{\mathcal B}(\mathcal A)$ by steps 3--5. The same criterion therefore supplies the inherited triangulated structure on both intersections.
